target.founder: Jonathan Hurst, Damion Shelton, Mikhail Jones

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series D → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.5x) to $5.2B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 5 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.0B - $2.3B.

private.name: Exotec
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series D), post-money $2B

data.narrative:
Agility Robotics, a Series D robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $400M+, was valued using two triangulation methods against a comparable universe of 9 private firms and 1 public company. The peer set includes five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Divergent (Series E, $2.3B), Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), Hadrian (Series C, $1.6B), Agile Robots (Series C, $1.0B), and Nimble Robotics (Series C, $1.0B).

Stage-progression methodology applies a 1.5x multiplier to the $5.2B total-raised proxy, yielding $7.8B. The peer-median method across the five comparables produces $1.6B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.3B. The disparity reflects differences in stage maturity and capital efficiency; Exotec at Series D commands a $2.0B valuation, while earlier-stage peers cluster at $1.0B–$1.6B.

Triangulating both methods produces a range of $1.4B (low) to $9.0B (high), with a median of $4.7B. The wide spread reflects tension between the stage-progression result, which treats total capital raised as a valuation proxy, and the peer-median result, which anchors to actual transaction prices. Key uncertainties include the applicability of the 1.5x step-up multiplier absent recent funding data, and heterogeneity in peer business models and go-to-market maturity.
